extraction_warnings: No individual participant sample-level data with complete identifiers were reported in the main text. The paper analyzes >6,500 metagenomes and reconstructs 1,023 P. copri genomes but does not provide sample-by-sample metadata. Samples extracted here represent the newly sequenced cohorts described in Methods (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Madagascar) and ancient samples mentioned explicitly. Individual-level metadata (age, sex, disease status) is reported only at the cohort/group level with means and ranges, not per-sample.

Ghana cohort: N=44 (23 adults, 25 children) with reported means and ranges; Ethiopia cohort: N=50 (24 adults, 26 infants); Tanzania cohort: N=68 (37 adults, 31 children). Specific participant identifiers and per-sample linkage to metagenome assemblies are not provided in the paper.

Ancient samples: The Iceman is a single 5,300-year-old mummy; three Mexican coprolites are from pre-Columbian site, two of which (2179 and 2180) had sufficient P. copri coverage for analysis. Radiocarbon dating for coprolite 2180 gives AD 673-768 (1284±16 BP).

All newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Madagascar) are classified as non-Westernized; all sampled individuals were healthy (free of self-reported disease). Ancient samples are assumed healthy by context.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Most schema fields are not applicable to this microbiome genomics study, which focuses on genetic diversity and population structure of Prevotella copri rather than clinical patient outcomes, treatments, or tumor staging.

The paper includes some disease-associated metadata from referenced cohorts (colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, IBD), but no patient-level disease response data is reported for the primary P. copri sequencing effort.
Study includes healthy subjects from Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania, plus neonates/infants, but no detailed neonatal parameters are reported beyond age ranges.
